For example sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as sound("bd").euclid(3,8), and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the same as sound("bd bd bd"). sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a groove somewhere between. Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

params.name: groove
params.description: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

chunks.title: every
chunks.text: An alias for firstOf

chunks.title: expand
chunks.text:
Experimental

Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

chunks.title: extend
chunks.text:
Experimental

extend is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".
examples: stepcat(  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),  sound("bd - sd -")).pace(8)

chunks.title: fadeTime
chunks.text: Used when using begin/end or chop/striate and friends, to change the fade out time of the 'grain' envelope.

chunks.title: fanchor
chunks.text: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2").lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

chunks.title: fast
chunks.text: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

chunks.title: fastChunk
chunks.text: Like chunk, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated for each set of chunks.

chunks.title: fastGap
chunks.text: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

chunks.title: filter
chunks.text: Filters haps using the given function

chunks.title: filterHaps
chunks.text: Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

params.name: hap_test
params.description: a function which returns false for haps to be removed from the pattern

chunks.title: filterValues
chunks.text: As with filterHaps, but the function is applied to values inside haps.
examples: const drums = s("bd sd bd sd")kick: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'bd').duck(2)snare: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'sd')bass: s("saw!4").note("G#1").lpf(80).lpenv(4).orbit(2)

chunks.title: filterWhen
chunks.text: Filters haps by their begin time

chunks.title: findPeaks
chunks.text: Find peaks in spectrum magnitudes

chunks.title: firstCycle
chunks.text: Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when debugging a pattern.

params.name: with_context
params.description: set to true, otherwise the context field will be stripped from the resulting haps.

chunks.title: firstCycleValues
chunks.text: Accessor for a list of values returned by querying the first cycle.

chunks.title: firstOf
chunks.text: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

chunks.title: fit
chunks.text: Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks. Similar to loopAt.

chunks.title: floor
chunks.text: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical floor. E.g. 3.7 replaced with to 3, and -4.2 replaced with -5.

chunks.title: fmap
chunks.text: see withValue

chunks.title: fmattack
chunks.text:
Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation

A number may be added afterwards to control the attack of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmatt5)
examples: note("c e g b g e").fm(4).fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")._scope()

chunks.title: fmdecay
chunks.text:
Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.

A number may be added afterwards to control the decay of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmdec6)
examples: note("c e g b g e").fm(4).fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>").fmsustain(.4)._scope()

chunks.title: fmenv
chunks.text:
Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..

A number may be added afterwards to control the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmenv4)
examples: note("c e g b g e").fm(4).fmdecay(.2).fmsustain(0).fmenv("<exp lin>")._scope()

chunks.title: fmh
chunks.text:
Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio. Controls the timbre of the sound. Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural, while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.

A number may be added afterwards to control the harmonicity of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmh2)
examples: note("c e g b g e").fm(4).fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")._scope()

chunks.title: fmi
chunks.text:
Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth. Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.

A number may be added afterwards to control the modulation index of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fm3). Also, FMs may be routed into each other with matrix commands like fm13, which would send fm1 back into fm3
examples: note("c e g b g e").fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")._scope()

chunks.title: fmrelease
chunks.text:
Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released

A number may be added afterwards to control the release of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmrel8)

chunks.title: fmsustain
chunks.text:
Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase

A number may be added afterwards to control the sustain of the envelope of any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmsus7)
examples: note("c e g b g e").fm(4).fmdecay(.1).fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")._scope()

chunks.title: fmwave
chunks.text:
Waveform of the fm modulator

A number may be added afterwards to control the waveform any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmwave6)

chunks.title: focus
chunks.text: Similar to compress, but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

chunks.title: fold
chunks.text: Wavefolding distortion

chunks.title: freq
chunks.text: Set frequency of sound.

params.name: frequency
params.description: in Hz. the audible range is between 20 and 20000 Hz

chunks.title: fromBipolar
chunks.text: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the unipolar range 0 .. 1

chunks.title: fscope
chunks.text: Renders an oscilloscope for the frequency domain of the audio signal.

params.name: color
params.description: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.description: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

chunks.title: ftranspose
chunks.text:
Frequency transpose. Assumes pattern either has freq set, or has values that can be interpreted as frequencies amt has optional edoSize param, defaults to 12. If haps have edoSize param set, such as from the output of xen("31edo"), ftrans will fallback to that instead of 12 as the default.

Transposes the frequency by amt edoSteps
examples: // to transpose by steps of an edo, use "step:edo" :i("0 7 8 18").xen("31edo").ftrans("<0 1:31 1:12>")
// it can also work with frequency values directlyfreq("200 300 400").ftrans("<0 7:31 7>")

chunks.title: ftype
chunks.text: Sets the filter type. The ladder filter is more aggressive. More types might be added in the future.
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)
note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2).sound('sawtooth').lpf(200).fanchor(0).lpenv(3).lpq(1).ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")

chunks.title: gain
chunks.text: Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

chunks.title: gap
chunks.text: Does absolutely nothing, but with a given metrical 'steps'

chunks.title: generateGraph
chunks.text: Creates a canvas element showing a graph of the given data.

params.name: data
params.description: An array of numbers, or a Float32Array.

params.name: min
params.description: Minimum value of data for the graph (lower edge).

params.name: max
params.description: Maximum value of data in the graph (upper edge).

chunks.title: generateReverb
chunks.text: Generates a reverb impulse response.

params.name: callback
params.description: Function to call when the impulse response has been generated. The impulse response is passed to this function as its parameter. May be called immediately within the current execution context, or later.

chunks.title: getDevice
chunks.text: Look up a device by index or name. Otherwise return a default device, or fail if none are connected.

chunks.title: getDur
chunks.text:
Returns the duration, in seconds, of the given sample. Has optional param n (for instance, the 2 in s("casio:2"))

Note: must be called with await, otherwise you'll get a pending Promise object.
examples: // Set a patterns cycle length to exactly the length of the samplesamples('github:tidalcycles/dirt-samples')let k = await getDuration('sax')s("sax").cps(1/k)

chunks.title: getMidiDeviceNamesString
chunks.text: Get a string listing device names for error messages.

chunks.title: gravityX
chunks.text: The device's gravity x-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: gravityY
chunks.text: The device's gravity y-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: gravityZ
chunks.text: The device's gravity z-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: grow
chunks.text:
Experimental

Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times. A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

chunks.title: handleOutputBuffersToRetrieve
chunks.text: Add contents of output buffers just processed to output buffers

chunks.title: hard
chunks.text: Hard-clipping distortion

chunks.title: hpattack
chunks.text: Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

chunks.title: hpdc
chunks.text: DC offset of the LFO for the highpass filter

chunks.title: hpdecay
chunks.text: Sets the decay duration for the highpass filter envelope.

chunks.title: hpdepth
chunks.text: Depth of the LFO for the highpass filter

chunks.title: hpdepthfrequency
chunks.text: Depth of the LFO for the hipass filter, in hz

chunks.title: hpenv
chunks.text: Sets the highpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.description: depth of the highpass filter envelope between 0 and n

chunks.title: hpf
chunks.text:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

chunks.title: hpq
chunks.text: Controls the high-pass q-value.

chunks.title: hprate
chunks.text: Rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

chunks.title: hprelease
chunks.text: Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

chunks.title: hpshape
chunks.text: Shape of the LFO for the highpass filter

chunks.title: hpskew
chunks.text: Skew of the LFO for the highpass filter

params.name: skew
params.description: How much to bend the LFO shape

chunks.title: hpsustain
chunks.text: Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

chunks.title: hpsync
chunks.text: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

chunks.title: hurry
chunks.text: Both speeds up the pattern (like 'fast') and the sample playback (like 'speed').

chunks.title: hush
chunks.text: Silences a pattern.

chunks.title: i
chunks.text: Selects the given degree. Currently used in xen and tune:

chunks.title: inhabit
chunks.text: Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to pick, but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.
examples: let a = s("bd(3,8)")let b = s("cp sd")"<a b [a,b]>".inhabit({ a, b })

chunks.title: inhabitmod
chunks.text: The same as inhabit, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

chunks.title: initDough
chunks.text: initializes dough ahead of time. you don't need to use this, but if you do, you can await it, so dough is ready before the pattern starts.

chunks.title: inside
chunks.text: Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

chunks.title: into
chunks.text: Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern. True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern to be played unchanged.

chunks.title: invert
chunks.text: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

chunks.title: irand
chunks.text: A continuous pattern of random integers, between 0 and n-1.
examples: // randomly select scale notes from 0 - 7 (= C to C)n(irand(8)).struct("x x*2 x x*3").scale("C:minor")

chunks.title: irbegin
chunks.text: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

chunks.title: iresponse
chunks.text: Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

chunks.title: irspeed
chunks.text: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

chunks.title: isaw
chunks.text: A sawtooth signal between 1 and 0 (like saw, but flipped).

chunks.title: isaw2
chunks.text: A sawtooth signal between 1 and -1 (like saw2, but flipped).

chunks.title: isquare
chunks.text: A square signal between 1 and 0 (like square but flipped).

chunks.title: isquare2
chunks.text: A square signal between 1 and -1 (like isquare, but bipolar).

chunks.title: iter
chunks.text: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

chunks.title: iterBack
chunks.text: Like iter, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

chunks.title: itri
chunks.text: An inverted triangle signal between 1 and 0 (like tri, but flipped).

chunks.title: itri2
chunks.text: An inverted triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like itri, but bipolar).

chunks.title: jux
chunks.text: The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(iter(4))

chunks.title: juxBy
chunks.text: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

chunks.title: juxFlip
chunks.text: Like jux, but flips the ears each cycle.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(iter(4))

chunks.title: juxFlipBy
chunks.text: Like juxBy, except it flips the ears each cycle.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlipBy(".8", rev)

chunks.title: keep
chunks.text:
When called on a pattern a, with a input pattern b (a.keep(b)), combines a and b such that anything defined in a, and anything defined in b that is not defined in a will be in the resulting pattern

The structure is maintained from a, because the default pattern alignment is in, see the section on Pattern Alignment in the technical manual in the docs

This is the inverse of set

See examples below
examples: // notes, already defined, will stay "c a f e",// while "s", not defined, will be set to "piano"note("c a f e").keep(note("e f a c").s("piano"))

chunks.title: keyDown
chunks.text: returns true when a key or array of keys is held Key name reference

chunks.title: label
chunks.text: Sets the displayed text for an event on the pianoroll

chunks.title: lastOf
chunks.text: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the last cycle.

chunks.title: late
chunks.text: Nudge a pattern to start later in time. Equivalent of Tidal's ~> operator

chunks.title: layer
chunks.text: Layers the result of the given function(s). Like superimpose, but without the original pattern:

chunks.title: leslie
chunks.text: Emulation of a Leslie speaker: speakers rotating in a wooden amplified cabinet.

chunks.title: lfo
chunks.text:
Configures an LFO. Can be called in sequence like pat.lfo(...).lfo(...) to set up multiple LFOs. There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

  1. Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. lfo({ c: "lpf" }))
  2. If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the lfo call will be used (e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).lfo() to modulate lpf)

Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside a sometimes. See example below.

params.name: config.subControl
params.description: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.dcoffset
params.description: DC offset / bias for the waveform. Aliases: dc

params.name: config.retrig
params.description: If > 0.5, the LFO will retrigger on each event. Aliases: rt

chunks.title: linger
chunks.text: Selects the given fraction of the pattern and repeats that part to fill the remainder of the cycle.

chunks.title: lock
chunks.text: Specifies whether delaytime is calculated relative to cps.

params.name: enable
params.description: When set to 1, delaytime is a direct multiple of a cycle.

chunks.title: log
chunks.text: Writes the content of the current event to the console (visible in the side menu).

chunks.title: logValues
chunks.text: A simplified version of log which writes all "values" (various configurable parameters) within the event to the console (visible in the side menu).

chunks.title: loop
chunks.text: Loops the sample. Note that the tempo of the loop is not synced with the cycle tempo. To change the loop region, use loopBegin / loopEnd.

chunks.title: loopAt
chunks.text: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles by changing the speed.

chunks.title: loopAtCps
chunks.text: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles and cps value, by changing the speed. deprecated: use loopAt or fit instead, together with setCps / setCpm.

chunks.title: loopBegin
chunks.text: Begin to loop at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end). Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and before loopEnd! Note: Samples starting with wt_ will automatically loop! (wt = wavetable)

params.name: time
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

chunks.title: loopEnd
chunks.text: End the looping section at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end). Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and after loopBegin!

params.name: time
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

chunks.title: lpattack
chunks.text: Sets the attack duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

chunks.title: lpdc
chunks.text: DC offset of the LFO for the lowpass filter

chunks.title: lpdecay
chunks.text: Sets the decay duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

chunks.title: lpdepth
chunks.text: Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter

chunks.title: lpdepthfrequency
chunks.text: Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter, in HZ

chunks.title: lpenv
chunks.text: Sets the lowpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.description: depth of the lowpass filter envelope between 0 and n

chunks.title: lpf
chunks.text:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'lpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

chunks.title: lpq
chunks.text: Controls the low-pass q-value.

chunks.title: lprate
chunks.text: Rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

chunks.title: lprelease
chunks.text: Sets the release time for the lowpass filter envelope.

chunks.title: lpshape
chunks.text: Shape of the LFO for the lowpass filter

chunks.title: lpskew
chunks.text: Skew of the LFO for the lowpass filter

params.name: skew
params.description: How much to bend the LFO shape

chunks.title: lpsustain
chunks.text: Sets the sustain amplitude for the lowpass filter envelope.

chunks.title: lpsync
chunks.text: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

chunks.title: lrate
chunks.text: Rate of modulation / rotation for leslie effect

chunks.title: lsize
chunks.text: Physical size of the cabinet in meters. Be careful, it might be slightly larger than your computer. Affects the Doppler amount (pitch warble)

chunks.title: markcss
chunks.text: Overrides the css of highlighted events. Make sure to use single quotes!

chunks.title: mask
chunks.text: Returns silence when mask is 0 or "~"

chunks.title: midi
chunks.text: MIDI output: Opens a MIDI output port.

params.name: midiport
params.description: MIDI device name or index defaulting to 0

chunks.title: midibend
chunks.text: MIDI pitch bend: Sends a MIDI pitch bend message.

chunks.title: midichan
chunks.text: MIDI channel: Sets the MIDI channel for the event.

chunks.title: midicmd
chunks.text: MIDI command: Sends a MIDI command message.

chunks.title: midikeys
chunks.text:
MIDI keyboard: Opens a MIDI input port to receive MIDI keyboard messages.

The note length is fixed as Superdough is not currently set up for undetermined note durations

The 'midichan' control value contains the number of the channel the note is coming from so it could be filtered or manipulated further in the chain.

params.name: input
params.description: MIDI device name or index defaulting to 0

examples: const kb = await midikeys('Arturia KeyStep 32')kb("0.5 1")  .s("saw")  .add(note(rand.mul(0.3)))  .lpf(1000).lpe(2).room(0.5)
// discard all notes not coming out from midi channel 2const kb = await midikeys('Arturia KeyStep 32')kb().filterValues(v=>v.midichan==2).s("tri")

chunks.title: midimaps
chunks.text: Adds midimaps to the registry. Inside each midimap, control names (e.g. lpf) are mapped to cc numbers.
examples: midimaps({ mymap: { lpf: 74 } })$: note("c a f e").lpf(sine.slow(4)).midimap('mymap').midi()
midimaps({ mymap: {  lpf: { ccn: 74, min: 0, max: 20000, exp: 0.5 }}})$: note("c a f e").lpf(sine.slow(2).range(400,2000)).midimap('mymap').midi()

chunks.title: midin
chunks.text:
MIDI input: Opens a MIDI input port to receive MIDI control change messages.

The output is a function that accepts a midi cc value to query as well as (optionally) a midi channel

params.name: input
params.description: MIDI device name or index defaulting to 0

examples: const cc = await midin('IAC Driver Bus 1')note("c a f e").lpf(cc(0).range(0, 1000)).lpq(cc(1).range(0, 10)).sound("sawtooth")
const allCC = await midin('IAC Driver Bus 1')const cc = (ccNum) => allCC(ccNum, 2) // just channel 2note("c a f e").s("saw")  .when(cc(0).gt(0), x => x.postgain(0))

chunks.title: midiport
chunks.text: MIDI port: Sets the MIDI port for the event.

chunks.title: miditouch
chunks.text: MIDI key after touch: Sends a MIDI key after touch message.

chunks.title: mode
chunks.text:
How the voicing is aligned to the anchor

  • below: top note <= anchor

  • duck: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded

  • above: bottom note >= anchor

  • root: bottom note is the lowest root of the chord >= anchor

  • oldabove : old (buggy) behavior of above, kept for legacy reason

  • oldroot : old (buggy) behavior of root, kept for legacy reason

params.name: modeName
params.description: one of {below | above | duck | root | oldabove | oldroot}

chunks.title: morph
chunks.text: Takes two binary rhythms represented as lists of 1s and 0s, and a number between 0 and 1 that morphs between them. The two lists should contain the same number of true values.
examples: sound("hh").struct(morph([1,0,1,0,1,0,1,0], // straight rhythm                         [1,1,0,1,0,1,0], // wonky rhythm                         0.25 // creates a slightly wonky rhythm                        )                  )

sound("hh").struct(morph("1:0:1:0:1:0:1:0", // straight rhythm                         "1:1:0:1:0:1:0", // wonky rhythm                         sine.slow(8) // slowly morph between the rhythms                        )                  )

chunks.title: mousex
chunks.text: The mouse's x position value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: mousey
chunks.text: The mouse's y position value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: mul
chunks.text: Multiplies each number by the given factor.

chunks.title: n
chunks.text:
Selects the given index:

  • for samples, it picks the sample by index, with wrap around
  • for scales, it picks the scale degree
  • for voicings, it picks the voice index

chunks.title: never
chunks.text: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0, fn) (never calls fn)

chunks.title: noise
chunks.text: Adds pink noise to the mix

chunks.title: note
chunks.text:
Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of

  • a letter (a-g or A-G)
  • optional accidentals (b or #)
  • optional (possibly negative) octave number (0-9). Defaults to 3

Examples of valid note names: c, bb, Bb, f#, c3, A4, Eb2, c#5

You can also use midi numbers instead of note names, where 69 is mapped to A4 440Hz in 12EDO.

chunks.title: nrpnn
chunks.text: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number message.

chunks.title: nrpv
chunks.text: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value message.

chunks.title: octave
chunks.text: Sets the default octave of a synth.

chunks.title: octaves
chunks.text: How many octaves are voicing steps spread apart, defaults to 1
examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").octaves("<2 4>").voicing()

chunks.title: off
chunks.text: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

chunks.title: offset
chunks.text: Sets how the voicing is offset from the anchored position

params.name: shift
params.description: the amount to shift the voicing up or down

examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").offset("<0 1 2 3 4 5>") // alter the voicing each time

chunks.title: often
chunks.text: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.75, fn)

chunks.title: onTriggerTime
chunks.text: make something happen on event time uses browser timeout which is innacurate for audio tasks

chunks.title: onsetsOnly
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern, with all haps without onsets filtered out. A hap with an onset is one with a whole timespan that begins at the same time as its part timespan.

chunks.title: orbit
chunks.text: An orbit is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

chunks.title: orientationAlpha
chunks.text: The device's orientation alpha value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: orientationBeta
chunks.text: The device's orientation beta value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: orientationGamma
chunks.text: The device's orientation gamma value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: osc
chunks.text: Sends each hap as an OSC message, which can be picked up by SuperCollider or any other OSC-enabled software. For more info, read MIDI & OSC in the docs

chunks.title: oschost
chunks.text: The host to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

chunks.title: oscport
chunks.text: The port to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

chunks.title: outside
chunks.text: Carries out an operation 'outside' a cycle.

chunks.title: pace
chunks.text:
Experimental

Speeds a pattern up or down, to fit to the given number of steps per cycle.
examples: sound("bd sd cp").pace(4)// The same as sound("{bd sd cp}%4") or sound("<bd sd cp>*4")

chunks.title: palindrome
chunks.text: Applies rev to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

chunks.title: pan
chunks.text: Sets position in stereo.

params.name: pan
params.description: between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)

examples: s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))

chunks.title: panchor
chunks.text:
Sets the range anchor of the envelope:

  • anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv]
  • anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note] If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

chunks.title: panspan
chunks.text: Controls how much multichannel output is fanned out

params.name: span
params.description: between -inf and inf, negative is backwards ordering

chunks.title: pansplay
chunks.text: Controls how much multichannel output is spread

chunks.title: parray
chunks.text: Turns a list of patterns into a single pattern which outputs list-values

chunks.title: partials
chunks.text:
Scale the magnitude of the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', ..)

Can also be used to create a new synth via s('user').partials(...)

params.name: magnitudes
params.description: List of [0, 1] magnitudes for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental harmonic (i.e. DC offset is skipped)

chunks.title: pattack
chunks.text: Attack time of pitch envelope.

chunks.title: pcurve
chunks.text: Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

chunks.title: pdecay
chunks.text: Decay time of pitch envelope.

chunks.title: penv
chunks.text: Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope. If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, pattack:.2 will be the default.

chunks.title: per
chunks.text: A pattern measuring the 'shortness' of events, or in other words, the duration of pattern events, in events per cycle. per doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with. For example per.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1") would give the same as "4 4 [8 8] 4". See also its reciprocal, cyclesPer.
examples: // Shorter events are more distortedn("0 0*2 0 0*2 0 [0 0 0]@2").sound("bd") .distort(per.div(2))

chunks.title: perlin
chunks.text: Generates a continuous pattern of perlin noise, in the range 0..1.

chunks.title: perx
chunks.text: Like per but measures the shortness of events according to an exponential curve. In particular, where the event duration halves, the returned value increases by one. perx.struct("1 1 [1 [1 1]] 1") would therefore be the same as "3 3 [4 [5 5]] 3".

chunks.title: phaser
chunks.text: Phaser audio effect that approximates popular guitar pedals.

chunks.title: phasercenter
chunks.text: The center frequency of the phaser in HZ. Defaults to 1000

chunks.title: phaserdepth
chunks.text: The amount the signal is affected by the phaser effect. Defaults to 0.75

chunks.title: phasersweep
chunks.text: The frequency sweep range of the lfo for the phaser effect. Defaults to 2000

chunks.title: phases
chunks.text: Rotates the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', 'user', ..) by a list of phases

params.name: phases
params.description: List of [0, 1) phases for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental phase (i.e. DC offset is skipped)

chunks.title: pianoroll
chunks.text: Visualises a pattern as a scrolling 'pianoroll', displayed in the background of the editor. To show a pianoroll for all running patterns, use all(pianoroll). To have a pianoroll appear below a pattern instead, prefix with _, e.g.: sound("bd sd")._pianoroll().

params.name: options
params.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to be displayed at the same time - defaults to 4

params.name: playhead
params.description: location of the active notes on the time axis - 0 to 1, defaults to 0.5

params.name: labels
params.description: displays labels on individual notes (see the label function) - 0 by default

params.name: flipTime
params.description: reverse the direction of the roll - 0 by default

params.name: flipValues
params.description: reverse the relative location of notes on the value axis - 0 by default

params.name: overscan
params.description: lookup X cycles outside of the cycles window to display notes in advance - 1 by default

params.name: hideNegative
params.description: hide notes with negative time (before starting playing the pattern) - 0 by default

params.name: smear
params.description: notes leave a solid trace - 0 by default

params.name: fold
params.description: notes takes the full value axis width - 0 by default

params.name: active
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the active notes - defaults to #FFCA28

params.name: inactive
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the inactive notes - defaults to #7491D2

params.name: background
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the background - defaults to transparent

params.name: playheadColor
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the line representing the play head - defaults to white

params.name: fill
params.description: notes are filled with color (otherwise only the label is displayed) - 0 by default

params.name: fillActive
params.description: active notes are filled with color - 0 by default

params.name: stroke
params.description: notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

params.name: strokeActive
params.description: active notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

params.name: hideInactive
params.description: only active notes are shown - 0 by default

params.name: colorizeInactive
params.description: use note color for inactive notes - 1 by default

params.name: fontFamily
params.description: define the font used by notes labels - defaults to 'monospace'

params.name: minMidi
params.description: minimum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 10

params.name: maxMidi
params.description: maximum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 90

params.name: autorange
params.description: automatically calculate the minMidi and maxMidi parameters - 0 by default

chunks.title: pick
chunks.text: Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to inhabit, but maintains the structure of the original patterns.
examples: note("<0 1 2!2 3>".pick(["g a", "e f", "f g f g" , "g c d"]))

chunks.title: pickAndRename
chunks.text: Selects entries from source and renames them via map

chunks.title: pickF
chunks.text: pickF lets you use a pattern of numbers to pick which function to apply to another pattern.

params.name: lookup
params.description: the array or lookup object of functions from which to pull

examples: note("<c2 d2>(3,8)").s("square").pickF("<jr l> f", { jr:jux(rev), f:fast(2), l:x=>x.lpf(800) })

chunks.title: pickOut
chunks.text: Similar to pick, but it applies an outerJoin instead of an innerJoin.

chunks.title: pickReset
chunks.text: Similar to pick, but the choosen pattern is reset when its index is triggered.

chunks.title: pickRestart
chunks.text: Similar to pick, but the choosen pattern is restarted when its index is triggered.

chunks.title: pickmod
chunks.text: The same as pick, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

chunks.title: pickmodF
chunks.text: The same as pickF, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the functions list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

params.name: lookup
params.description: the array or lookup object of functions from which to pull

chunks.title: pickmodOut
chunks.text: The same as pickOut, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

chunks.title: pickmodReset
chunks.text: The same as pickReset, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

chunks.title: pickmodRestart
chunks.text: The same as pickRestart, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

chunks.title: pitchwheel
chunks.text: Renders a pitch circle to visualize frequencies within one octave

chunks.title: ply
chunks.text: The ply function repeats each event the given number of times.

chunks.title: plyForEach
chunks.text: The plyForEach function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event. This version of ply uses the iteration index as an argument to the function, similar to echoWith.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

chunks.title: plyWith
chunks.text: The plyWith function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.\n

chunks.title: polymeter
chunks.text:
Experimental

Aligns the steps of the patterns, creating polymeters. The patterns are repeated until they all fit the cycle. For example, in the below the first pattern is repeated twice, and the second is repeated three times, to fit the lowest common multiple of six steps.
examples: // The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

chunks.title: postgain
chunks.text: Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

chunks.title: prelease
chunks.text: Release time of pitch envelope
examples: note("<c eb g bb> ~").release(.5) // to hear the pitch release.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")

chunks.title: prepareInputBuffersToSend
chunks.text: Copy contents of input buffers to buffer actually sent to process

chunks.title: press
chunks.text: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.
examples: stack(s("hh*4"),      s("bd mt sd ht").every(4, press)     ).slow(2)

chunks.title: pressBy
chunks.text: Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

chunks.title: progNum
chunks.text: MIDI program number: Sends a MIDI program change message.

chunks.title: pure
chunks.text: A discrete value that repeats once per cycle.

chunks.title: pw
chunks.text: Controls the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

chunks.title: pwrate
chunks.text: Controls the lfo rate for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

chunks.title: pwsweep
chunks.text: Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

chunks.title: queryArc
chunks.text: Query haps inside the given time span.
examples: const pattern = sequence('a', ['b', 'c'])const haps = pattern.queryArc(0, 1)console.log(haps)silence

chunks.title: rand
chunks.text: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between 0 and 1.

chunks.title: rand2
chunks.text: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between -1 and 1

chunks.title: randL
chunks.text: Creates a list of random numbers of the given length

chunks.title: range
chunks.text: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range. Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

chunks.title: range2
chunks.text: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

chunks.title: rangex
chunks.text: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range, following an exponential curve.

chunks.title: rarely
chunks.text: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.25, fn)

chunks.title: ratio
chunks.text: Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":". Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

chunks.title: readInputs
chunks.text: Read next web audio block to input buffers

chunks.title: reallocateChannelsIfNeeded
chunks.text: Handles dynamic reallocation of input/output channels buffer (channel numbers may vary during lifecycle)

chunks.title: ref
chunks.text: exposes a custom value at query time. basically allows mutating state without evaluation

chunks.title: register
chunks.text: Registers a new pattern method. The method is added to the Pattern class + the standalone function is returned from register.

params.name: name
params.description: name of the function, or an array of names to be used as synonyms

params.name: func
params.description: function with 1 or more params, where last is the current pattern

params.name: patternify
params.description: defaults to true; if set to false, you will have more control over the arguments to func as they will be in their raw form and it will be up to you to patternify them and/or query them for values

examples: const vlpf = register('vlpf', (freq, pat) => {  return pat.fmap((v) => ({...v, cutoff: freq * (v.velocity ?? 1) }));})s("saw").seg(8).velocity(rand).vlpf(800)

chunks.title: release
chunks.text: Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

chunks.title: removeUndefineds
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern, with haps containing undefined values removed from query results.

chunks.title: repeatCycles
chunks.text: Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

chunks.title: replicate
chunks.text:
Experimental

replicate is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".replicate(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".

TODO: find out how this function differs from extend
examples: stepcat(  sound("bd bd - cp").replicate(2),  sound("bd - sd -")).pace(8)

chunks.title: reset
chunks.text: Resets the pattern to the start of the cycle for each onset of the reset pattern.

chunks.title: restart
chunks.text: Restarts the pattern for each onset of the restart pattern. While reset will only reset the current cycle, restart will start from cycle 0.

chunks.title: rev
chunks.text: Reverse all cycles in a pattern. See also revv for reversing a whole pattern.

chunks.title: revv
chunks.text: Reverse a whole pattern. See also rev for reversing each cycle.
examples: // This is the same as `<[g e] [d c]>`. If `rev()` is used, you get// the same as `<[d c] [g e]>`, where each cycle reverses, but the order of// cycles stays the same.note("<[c d] [e g]>").revv()

chunks.title: ribbon
chunks.text: Loops the pattern inside an offset for cycles. If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

chunks.title: room
chunks.text:
Sets the level of reverb.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

chunks.title: roomdim
chunks.text: Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

chunks.title: roomfade
chunks.text: Reverb fade time (in seconds). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

chunks.title: roomlp
chunks.text: Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

chunks.title: roomsize
chunks.text: Sets the room size of the reverb, see room. When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

chunks.title: rootNotes
chunks.text: Maps the chords of the incoming pattern to root notes in the given octave.

chunks.title: rotationAlpha
chunks.text: The device's rotation around the alpha-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: rotationBeta
chunks.text: The device's rotation around the beta-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: rotationGamma
chunks.text: The device's rotation around the gamma-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

chunks.title: round
chunks.text: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded to the nearest integer.

chunks.title: run
chunks.text: A discrete pattern of numbers from 0 to n-1

chunks.title: s
chunks.text: Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters separated by ':'.

params.name: sound
params.description: The sound / pattern of sounds to pick

chunks.title: samples
chunks.text: Loads a collection of samples to use with s
examples: samples({ bd: '808bd/BD0000.WAV', sd: '808sd/SD0010.WAV' }, 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidalcycles/Dirt-Samples/master/');s("[bd ~]*2, [~ hh]*2, ~ sd")

chunks.title: saw
chunks.text: A sawtooth signal between 0 and 1.

chunks.title: saw2
chunks.text: A sawtooth signal between -1 and 1 (like saw, but bipolar).

chunks.title: scale
chunks.text:
Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale.

When describing notes via numbers, note that negative numbers can be used to wrap backwards in the scale as well as sharps or flats to produce notes outside of the scale.

Also sets scale for other scale operations, like {@link Pattern#scaleTranspose}.

A scale consists of a root note (e.g. c4, c, f#, bb4) followed by semicolon (':') and then a scale type.

The scale name must be written without spaces (because it would be interpreted as a multi-step pattern otherwise). If your scale name includes spaces, replace them with colons.

The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

chunks.title: scaleTranspose
chunks.text: Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps. Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a {@link Pattern#scale}

chunks.title: scope
chunks.text: Renders an oscilloscope for the time domain of the audio signal.

params.name: align
params.description: if 1, the scope will be aligned to the first zero crossing. defaults to 1

params.name: color
params.description: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.description: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

params.name: trigger
params.description: amplitude value that is used to align the scope. defaults to 0.

chunks.title: scramble
chunks.text: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to shuffle, but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

chunks.title: scrub
chunks.text: Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

chunks.title: seed
chunks.text: Change the seed for random signals. Normally, random signals depend on time, so two patterns at the same time will have the same random values. Specifying a new seed changes the signal output by rand. This also affects other functions that use randomness, like shuffle and sometimes.

params.name: n
params.description: A new seed. Can be any number.

examples: $: s("hh*4").degrade();$: s("bd*4").degrade().seed(1); // Will degrade different events from the hi-hat

chunks.title: segment
chunks.text: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

chunks.title: seq
chunks.text: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.
examples: // As a chained function:s("hh*4").seq(  note("c4(5,8)"))

chunks.title: seqPLoop
chunks.text: Similarly to arrange, allows you to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles. Unlike arrange, you specify a start and stop time for each pattern rather than duration, which means that patterns can overlap.

chunks.title: sequence
chunks.text: See fastcat

chunks.title: sequenceP
chunks.text: Takes a list of patterns, and returns a pattern of lists.

chunks.title: set
chunks.text:
When called on a pattern a, with a input pattern b (a.set(b)), combines a and b such that anything defined in b and anything defined in a that is not defined in b will be in the resulting pattern.

The structure is maintained from a, because the default pattern alignment is in, see the section on Pattern Alignment in the technical manual in the docs

This is the inverse of keep

See examples below
examples: // because input pattern has `s` set,// it overrides the "sine" declared earliernote("c a f e").s("sine").set(s("triangle"))

chunks.title: setContext
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

chunks.title: setDefaultJoin
chunks.text:
Sets the default method of combining events from two patterns (aka alignment) in Strudel. The default method is 'in', meaning that patterns to the left will (typically) dictate the event timings when combined with patterns to the right. By changing alignment to 'out', the opposite will happen. With 'mix', they will combine their event timings.

Note that we say the default method, because alignments can also be set explicitly with calls like 'add.mix', 'set.squeeze', etc.
examples: setDefaultJoin('mix') // also try 'in', 'out', 'squeeze', etc.s("saw").vel("1 0.5").note("F A C E").delay("0 0.2 0.3")

chunks.title: setGainCurve
chunks.text: Apply a function to all gains provided in patterns. Can be used to rescale gain to be quadratic, exponential, etc. rather than linear
examples: setGainCurve((x) => x * x) // quadratic gains("bd*4").gain(0.5) // equivalent to 0.25 gain normally

chunks.title: setMaxPolyphony
chunks.text: Set the max polyphony. If notes are ringing out via release then they will start to die out in first-in-first-out order once the max polyphony has been hit

chunks.title: setcpm
chunks.text: Changes the global tempo to the given cycles per minute

chunks.title: shape
chunks.text: (Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud. Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

chunks.title: shiftInputBuffers
chunks.text: Shift left content of input buffers to receive new web audio block

chunks.title: shiftOutputBuffers
chunks.text: Shift left content of output buffers to receive new web audio block

chunks.title: shiftPeaks
chunks.text: Shift peaks and regions of influence by pitchFactor into new specturm

chunks.title: showFirstCycle
chunks.text: More human-readable version of the firstCycleValues accessor.

chunks.title: shrink
chunks.text:
Experimental

Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times. A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

chunks.title: shuffle
chunks.text: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order. Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

chunks.title: silence
chunks.text: Does absolutely nothing..

chunks.title: sine
chunks.text: A sine signal between 0 and 1.

chunks.title: sine2
chunks.text: A sine signal between -1 and 1 (like sine, but bipolar).

chunks.title: sinefold
chunks.text: Wavefolding distortion composed with sinusoid

chunks.title: slice
chunks.text: Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers. Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

chunks.title: slider
chunks.text: Displays a slider widget to allow the user manipulate a value

chunks.title: slow
chunks.text: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

chunks.title: slowcat
chunks.text: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

chunks.title: slowcatPrime
chunks.text: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle. Unlike slowcat, this version will skip cycles.

chunks.title: soft
chunks.text: Soft-clipping distortion

chunks.title: someCycles
chunks.text: Shorthand for .someCyclesBy(0.5, fn)

chunks.title: someCyclesBy
chunks.text: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis. Similar to sometimesBy

chunks.title: sometimes
chunks.text: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

chunks.title: sometimesBy
chunks.text: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability. Similar to someCyclesBy

chunks.title: sortHapsByPart
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern, which returns haps sorted in temporal order. Mainly of use when comparing two patterns for equality, in tests.

chunks.title: soundAlias
chunks.text: Register an alias for a sound.

params.name: alias
params.description: The alias to use for the sound

chunks.title: source
chunks.text: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

chunks.title: spectrum
chunks.text: Renders a spectrum analyzer for the incoming audio signal.

chunks.title: speed
chunks.text: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: speed
params.description: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

chunks.title: spiral
chunks.text: Displays a spiral visual.

params.name: options
params.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: stretch
params.description: controls the rotations per cycle ratio, where 1 = 1 cycle / 360 degrees

params.name: cap
params.description: style of line ends: butt (default), round, square

params.name: playheadLength
params.description: length of playhead in rotations, defaults to 0.02

params.name: steady
params.description: steadyness of spiral vs playhead. 1 = spiral doesn't move, playhead does.

params.name: activeColor
params.description: color of active segment. defaults to foreground of theme

params.name: inactiveColor
params.description: color of inactive segments. defaults to gutterForeground of theme

params.name: colorizeInactive
params.description: wether or not to colorize inactive segments, defaults to 0

params.name: fade
params.description: wether or not past and future should fade out. defaults to 1

params.name: logSpiral
params.description: wether or not the spiral should be logarithmic. defaults to 0

chunks.title: splice
chunks.text: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

chunks.title: splitQueries
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to happen within a cycle.

chunks.title: spread
chunks.text: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

chunks.title: square
chunks.text: A square signal between 0 and 1.

chunks.title: square2
chunks.text: A square signal between -1 and 1 (like square, but bipolar).

chunks.title: squeeze
chunks.text: Pick from the list of values (or patterns of values) via the index using the given pattern of integers. The selected pattern will be compressed to fit the duration of the selecting event
examples: note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))

chunks.title: squiz
chunks.text:
Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as:

"A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

params.name: squiz
params.description: Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.

chunks.title: stack
chunks.text: The given items are played at the same time at the same length.
examples: // As a chained function:s("hh*4").stack(  note("c4(5,8)"))

chunks.title: stepalt
chunks.text:
Experimental

Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'. Similar to stepcat, but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.
examples: stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()

chunks.title: stepcat
chunks.text: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle. The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair. Has the alias timecat.
examples: stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()

chunks.title: stretch
chunks.text: Changes the pitch of the sample without changing its speed. The frequencies are multiplied by (factor + 1) for positive numbers and by max(factor / 4 + 1, 0) for negative numbers. So tuning up by octaves can be done with 1, 3, 7, ... and tuning down by octaves with -2, -3, -3.5...

params.name: factor
params.description: between -4 and inf. Positive increases pitch, 0 does nothing, negative decreases the pitch.

chunks.title: striate
chunks.text: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

chunks.title: stripContext
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern with the context field of every hap set to an empty object.

chunks.title: struct
chunks.text: Applies the given structure to the pattern:
examples: note("c,eb,g")  .struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~")  .slow(2)

chunks.title: stut
chunks.text: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

chunks.title: sub
chunks.text: Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.
examples: n("0 2 4".sub("<0 1 2 3>")).scale("C4:minor")// See add for more information.

chunks.title: superimpose
chunks.text: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

chunks.title: sustain
chunks.text: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

chunks.title: swing
chunks.text: Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

chunks.title: swingBy
chunks.text: The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if x is 0 it does nothing, 0.5 delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

chunks.title: sysex
chunks.text: MIDI sysex: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

chunks.title: sysexdata
chunks.text: MIDI sysex data: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

chunks.title: sysexid
chunks.text: MIDI sysex ID: Sends a MIDI sysex identifier message.

chunks.title: tables
chunks.text: Loads a collection of wavetables to use with s

chunks.title: tag
chunks.text: Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering. The function populates Hap.context.tags (Array).
examples: s("saw!16").note("F1")  .lpf(tri.range(40, 80).slow(4)).lpenv(5).lpq(4).lpd(0.15)  .when(rand.late(0.1).gte(0.5), x => x.transpose("12").tag('altered'))  .when(rand.late(0.2).gte(0.5), x => x.s("square").tag('altered'))  .when("<0 1>", x => x.filter((hap) => hap.hasTag('altered')))

chunks.title: take
chunks.text:
Experimental

Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest). A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.
examples: "bd cp ht mt".take("2").sound()// The same as "bd cp".sound()
"bd cp ht mt".take("1 2 3").sound()// The same as "bd bd cp bd cp ht".sound()
"bd cp ht mt".take("-1 -2 -3").sound()// The same as "mt ht mt cp ht mt".sound()

chunks.title: time
chunks.text: A signal representing the cycle time.

chunks.title: timecat
chunks.text: Aliases for stepcat

chunks.title: toBipolar
chunks.text:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 ..

  1. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the bipolar range -1 .. 1

chunks.title: tour
chunks.text:
Experimental

Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

chunks.title: transient
chunks.text: Transient shaper. Gives independent control over the emphasis on transients and sustains

chunks.title: transpose
chunks.text:
Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values. The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation. If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with

  • M = major
  • m = minor
  • P = perfect
  • A = augmented
  • d = diminished

Examples intervals:

  • 1P = unison
  • 3M = major third
  • 3m = minor third
  • 4P = perfect fourth
  • 4A = augmented fourth
  • 5P = perfect fifth
  • 5d = diminished fifth

params.name: amount
params.description: Either number of semitones or interval string.

chunks.title: tremolo
chunks.text: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

chunks.title: tremolodepth
chunks.text: Depth of amplitude modulation

chunks.title: tremolophase
chunks.text: Alter the phase of the modulation waveform

params.name: offset
params.description: the offset in cycles of the modulation

chunks.title: tremoloshape
chunks.text: Shape of amplitude modulation
examples: note("{f g c d}%16").tremsync(4).tremoloshape("<sine tri square>").s("sawtooth")

chunks.title: tremoloskew
chunks.text: Alter the shape of the modulation waveform

chunks.title: tremolosync
chunks.text: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

chunks.title: tri
chunks.text: A triangle signal between 0 and 1.

chunks.title: tri2
chunks.text: A triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like tri, but bipolar).

chunks.title: tune
chunks.text: Assumes pattern contains numerical scale degrees on the i control (see examples below). Accepts a scale name or list of frequencies (see all available names at the link on the reference). Returns a new pattern with all values mapped to a frequency ratio. Similar to xen.
examples: // You can set your root to be a// particular note with getFreq:i("4 8 9 10 - - 5 7 9 11 - -").tune("tranh3")  .mul(getFreq('c3'))  .freq().clip(.5).room(1)

chunks.title: undegrade
chunks.text: Inverse of degrade: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .undegradeBy(0.5) Events that would be removed by degrade are let through by undegrade and vice versa (see second example).

chunks.title: undegradeBy
chunks.text: Inverse of degradeBy: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 100% chance of removal 1 = 0% chance of removal Events that would be removed by degradeBy are let through by undegradeBy and vice versa (see second example).

chunks.title: unison
chunks.text: Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators.
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")

chunks.title: unit
chunks.text: Used in conjunction with speed, accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using unit "c" means speed will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. speed "1" means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using unit "s" means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by speed.

chunks.title: useRNG
chunks.text: Sets which random number generator to use. Historically Strudel would use useRNG('legacy'), which remains the default. To use a new more statistically precise RNG, try useRNG('precise').

chunks.title: velocity
chunks.text: Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

chunks.title: vib
chunks.text: Applies a vibrato to the frequency of the oscillator.
examples: // change the modulation depth with ":"note("a e").vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>:12")._scope()

chunks.title: vibmod
chunks.text: Sets the vibrato depth in semitones. Only has an effect if vibrato | vib | v is is also set
examples: // change the vibrato frequency with ":"note("a e").vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>:8")._scope()

chunks.title: voicing
chunks.text:
Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params:

  • chord: Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7
  • dict: voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary
  • anchor: the note that is used to align the chord
  • mode: how the voicing is aligned to the anchor
    • below: top note <= anchor
    • duck: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded
    • above: bottom note >= anchor
    • root: bottom note is the lowest root of the chord >= anchor
    • oldabove : old (buggy) behavior of above, kept for legacy reason
    • oldroot : old (buggy) behavior of root, kept for legacy reason
  • offset: whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing
  • n: if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved

All of the above controls are optional, except chord. If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.

chunks.title: voicings
chunks.text: DEPRECATED: still works, but it is recommended you use .voicing instead (without s). Turns chord symbols into voicings, using the smoothest voice leading possible. Uses chord-voicings package.
examples: stack("<C^7 A7 Dm7 G7>".voicings('lefthand'), "<C3 A2 D3 G2>").note()

chunks.title: vowel
chunks.text: Formant filter to make things sound like vowels.

params.name: vowel
params.description: You can use a e i o u ae aa oe ue y uh un en an on, corresponding to [a] [e] [i] [o] [u] [æ] [ɑ] [ø] [y] [ɯ] [ʌ] [œ̃] [ɛ̃] [ɑ̃] [ɔ̃]. Aliases: aa = å = ɑ, oe = ø = ö, y = ı, ae = æ.

examples: s("bd sd mt ht bd [~ cp] ht lt").vowel("[a|e|i|o|u]")

chunks.title: warp
chunks.text: Amount of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator

chunks.title: warpattack
chunks.text: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

chunks.title: warpdc
chunks.text: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

chunks.title: warpdecay
chunks.text: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

chunks.title: warpdepth
chunks.text: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

chunks.title: warpenv
chunks.text: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

chunks.title: warpmode
chunks.text:
Type of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator.

The current options are: none, asym, bendp, bendm, bendmp, sync, quant, fold, pwm, orbit, spin, chaos, primes, binary, brownian, reciprocal, wormhole, logistic, sigmoid, fractal, flip
examples: s("morgana").bank("wt_digital").seg(8).note("F1").warp("0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1")  .warpmode("<asym bendp spin logistic sync wormhole brownian>*2")

chunks.title: warprate
chunks.text: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

chunks.title: warprelease
chunks.text: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

chunks.title: warpshape
chunks.text: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

chunks.title: warpskew
chunks.text: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

params.name: skew
params.description: How much to bend the LFO shape

chunks.title: warpsustain
chunks.text: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

chunks.title: warpsync
chunks.text: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable warp position

chunks.title: wchoose
chunks.text: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements by giving a probability to each element

chunks.title: wchooseCycles
chunks.text: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle by giving a probability to each element
examples: wchooseCycles(["c c c",5], ["a a a",3], ["f f f",1]).fast(4).note()
// The probability can itself be a patternwchooseCycles(["bd(3,8)","<5 0>"], ["hh hh hh",3]).fast(4).s()

chunks.title: when
chunks.text: Applies the given function whenever the given pattern is in a true state.

chunks.title: whenKey
chunks.text: Do something on a keypress, or array of keypresses Key name reference

chunks.title: withBase
chunks.text: Assumes pattern of frequencies tuned to some base frequency, such as the output of xen Because xen defaults to 220Hz, so will withBase. but you can specify a different original base with the standard optional array syntax ':'

chunks.title: withContext
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the context field of every hap.

chunks.title: withHap
chunks.text: As with withHaps, but applies the function to every hap, rather than every list of haps.

chunks.title: withHapSpan
chunks.text: Similar to withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to the timespans of all haps returned by pattern queries (both part timespans, and where present, whole timespans).

chunks.title: withHapTime
chunks.text: As with withHapSpan, but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the hap timespans.

chunks.title: withHaps
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the list of haps returned by every query.

chunks.title: withLoc
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern with the given location information added to the context of every hap.

chunks.title: withQuerySpan
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern, where the given function is applied to the query timespan before passing it to the original pattern.

chunks.title: withQueryTime
chunks.text: As with withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the query timespan.

chunks.title: withSeed
chunks.text: Modify a pattern by applying a function to the randomSeed control if present

params.name: func
params.description: Function from seed (or undefined) to seed (or undefined)

chunks.title: withValue
chunks.text: Returns a new pattern, with the function applied to the value of each hap. It has the alias fmap.

chunks.title: within
chunks.text: Use within to apply a function to only a part of a pattern.

params.name: func
params.description: function to be applied to the sub-pattern

chunks.title: wordfall
chunks.text: Displays a vertical pianoroll with event labels. Supports all the same options as pianoroll.

chunks.title: worklet
chunks.text: Creates a worklet effect. Typically derived by writing K(...) in the REPL which will parse Kabelsalat code.

params.name: src
params.description: Source code of the worklet update function

chunks.title: writeOutputs
chunks.text: Write next web audio block from output buffers

chunks.title: wt
chunks.text: Position in the wavetable of the wavetable oscillator

chunks.title: wtattack
chunks.text: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

chunks.title: wtdc
chunks.text: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

chunks.title: wtdecay
chunks.text: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

chunks.title: wtdepth
chunks.text: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

chunks.title: wtenv
chunks.text: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

chunks.title: wtphaserand
chunks.text: Amount of randomness of the initial phase of the wavetable oscillator.

params.name: amount
params.description: Randomness of the initial phase. Between 0 (not random) and 1 (fully random)

chunks.title: wtrate
chunks.text: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

chunks.title: wtrelease
chunks.text: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

chunks.title: wtshape
chunks.text: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

chunks.title: wtskew
chunks.text: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

params.name: skew
params.description: How much to bend the LFO shape

chunks.title: wtsustain
chunks.text: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

chunks.title: wtsync
chunks.text: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

chunks.title: xen
chunks.text: Assumes a numerical pattern of scale steps, and a scale. Scales accepted are all preset scale names of tune, arbitrary edos such as 31edo, or an array of frequency ratios. Assumes scales repeat at octave (2/1). Returns a new pattern with all values mapped to their associated frequency, assuming a base frequency of 220hz.
examples: // You can also use xen with frequency ratios.// This is equivalent to the above:i("0 1 2").xen([  Math.pow(2, 0/31),  Math.pow(2, 8/31),  Math.pow(2, 18/31),]).piano()
// xen also supports all scale names that// tune does:i("0 1 2 3 4 5").xen("hexany15")// equiv to:// "0 1 2 3 4 5".tune("hexany15").mul("220").freq()

chunks.title: xfade
chunks.text:
Cross-fades between left and right from 0 to 1:

  • 0 = (full left, no right)
  • .5 = (both equal)
  • 1 = (no left, full right)

chunks.title: zip
chunks.text:
Experimental

'zips' together the steps of the provided patterns. This can create a long repetition, taking place over a single, dense cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
zip("e f", "e f g", "g [f e] a f4 c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

chunks.title: zoom
chunks.text: Plays a portion of a pattern, specified by the beginning and end of a time span. The new resulting pattern is played over the time period of the original pattern:
examples: s("bd*2 hh*3 [sd bd]*2 perc").zoom(0.25, 0.75)// s("hh*3 [sd bd]*2") // equivalent
